A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same authors' BLIP-based segmentation framework and LLM evaluator, despite renaming. All pages, including equations, tables, figures and appendices, are readable and support comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original segmentation results on VOC, ADE20K and Cityscapes, including quantitative comparisons, captioning-cycle ablations and qualitative examples.

after.justification: v2 reports original segmentation experiments, including added PASCAL Context results and SAM/LLaVA comparisons in Appendix B, alongside ablations and qualitative outputs.

M1.justification: Section 3.1 expands the specified clustering ensemble from four assignments using k=2 and 8 at two resolutions to fourteen assignments using k=2 through 8. The clustering, alignment, denoising, caption filtering and segmentation pipeline otherwise remains intact. SELF-SEG becoming AutoSeg and LOVE becoming LAVE are renamings.

E1.justification: v2 adds PASCAL Context with 459 classes throughout evaluation. This tests substantially broader annotations on images shared with VOC, while retaining VOC, ADE20K, Cityscapes and the same segmentation task; it extends coverage within the existing image domains.

E2.justification: Appendix B and Table 4 add SAM + BLIP + X-Decoder and LLaVA + X-Decoder as directly evaluated automatic-vocabulary comparators on VOC, Context and Cityscapes. These substantially broaden comparisons addressing the central class-generation contribution. The original main-table comparator membership and VLM-ablation comparator set are retained.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 changes the reported X-Decoder configuration from Focal-T to Focal-L and clustering from k={2,8} to k=2 through 8. Appendix B introduces SAM object-proposal captioning and prompted LLaVA evaluation procedures. These materially change experimental configurations; mIoU and cmIoU remain the metrics, and cross-version scores are not same-setting comparisons.

E4.justification: v2 adds a focused comparison testing alternative class generators and revises the qualitative failure cases, including compound-noun parsing, mosque/temple confusion and dominant-class oversegmentation. Both original ablation questions remain. Appendix C's intermediate clustering visualization largely redisplays evidence already shown in v1 Figure 3.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run estimates, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. Repeated captioning cycles are part of the inference procedure, not newly introduced statistical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: v1 Table 2's VOC/ADE20K/Cityscapes mIoUs of 41.6/6.4/41.1 are replaced by 87.1/5.9/29.5 in v2 Table 3 under revised settings, with Context added at 11.7. VOC cmIoU changes from 41.9 to 71.8 in Table 1. Caption-cycle optima change from 1/10/20 to 10/1/25 for the retained datasets. New comparator results and qualitative outputs are added; existing main-table baseline scores on the original datasets remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The transformer definitions change substantively: v1 Equations (5)–(6) normalize after residual addition, whereas v2 Equations (4)–(5) place normalization inside the attention/MLP branches. This revises the mathematical description without establishing that the pretrained BLIP implementation changed. Other clustering and filtering definitions are essentially retained, with no new proofs or theorems.

C1.justification: Both versions claim automatic class discovery and segmentation without additional training or user-specified categories, introduce BCC and an LLM evaluator, and claim strong automatic-vocabulary performance competitive with conventional OVS. Naming the task AVS and adding Context evidence do not fundamentally alter these contributions.

C2.justification: v2 interprets ADE20K's one-cycle optimum as efficient handling of complex scenes, suggests redundant generated nouns explain alternative-baseline false positives, and adds noun-parsing and class-dominance failure explanations. It removes v1's specific warning that unannotated VOC objects may distort the apparent optimal cycle count. Low-resolution mask and competing-noun limitations remain.

D1.justification: v2's abstract adds a code-repository hyperlink and states that code is available, replacing v1's release promise, although its introduction retains future-tense wording. It documents SAM prompting, the LLaVA noun-list prompt and Context mapping instructions, and repairs the ADE20K prompt's opening question. The existing LLM Mapper pseudocode is retained and relocated.

R1.justification: v2 adds references for SAM, LLaVA, PASCAL Context and Attention Is All You Need, with corresponding discussion of alternative captioning approaches. The broader positioning against OVS and ZeroSeg remains intact. OpenSeg's revised reference title identifies the same work rather than a new citation.

P1.justification: v2 renames the paper, task, framework and evaluator, rewrites the abstract and several experimental passages, adds explicit evaluation/implementation headings, and reorganizes the appendices into A–D. The main section sequence and much of the method and related-work narrative remain recognizable.

P2.justification: The document changes from two-column to single-column layout, redraws the method overview, replaces the introductory example display, expands the qualitative grid and adds Context columns and a new comparison table. Individual appendix figures are regrouped into dataset-specific panels, while intermediate clustering outputs move into a separate appendix figure.

improvement.justification: Context evaluation, direct SAM/LLaVA comparisons, additional failure explanations and code-access information make v2 better substantiated and more useful. These gains are tempered by the removed VOC annotation caveat and reporting inconsistencies: the stated 86% relative VOC performance does not match Table 3's 87.1/97.2, approximately 90%. Changed experimental configurations also prevent interpreting the higher VOC score as a same-setting methodological improvement.
